{"id": 175, "title": "Discovery-retrieval pack — Dunmore Pell LLP settlement offer letter to Harwick & Sloane (2025-07-22)", "doc_type": "input_materials", "related_shape": "discovery-retrieval", "body": "DUNMORE PELL LLP
Counselors at Law — Saint Paul
July 22, 2025

BY EMAIL — SUBJECT TO FED. R. EVID. 408 AND ALL STATE ANALOGUES
Adaeze Reyes, Esq.
Harwick & Sloane LLP
Counsel for Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc.

Re: Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877 — offer of compromise

Dear Ms. Reyes:

This letter is a confidential offer of compromise made solely to avoid the burden and expense of continued litigation. Nothing in it is or may be construed as an admission of liability, fault, or the truth of any allegation in the complaint, all of which Talvern Logistics Group LLC continues to deny.

On behalf of Talvern, we are authorized to offer 2,100,000 dollars, payable within thirty days of execution of a settlement agreement, in full and final settlement of all claims that were or could have been asserted in the above-captioned action, conditioned on: (a) a complete mutual release of all claims arising from or relating to the Warehousing and Climate Services Agreement and the storage of the cooperative's grain at Silo Complex 4; (b) dismissal of the action with prejudice, each party to bear its own fees and costs; (c) withdrawal of the cooperative's pending preservation and spoliation correspondence and any contemplated motion practice thereon; and (d) customary confidentiality and non-disparagement terms.

In our client's view this offer should be measured against the genuine disputes in the case, including causation of the claimed grading outcomes, the cooperative's own monitoring obligations under Section 4.7 of the agreement, and the substantial cost both parties face through expert discovery and trial.

This offer remains open for twenty-one days from the date of this letter, after which it is withdrawn without further notice. It may be accepted only in a writing signed by our client.

Very truly yours,
Jonas Pell
Dunmore Pell LLP
Counsel for Talvern Logistics Group LLC"}

{"id": 174, "title": "Discovery-retrieval pack — Meridian special board meeting minutes: settlement authority vote (2025-08-01)", "doc_type": "input_materials", "related_shape": "discovery-retrieval", "body": "MERIDIAN GRAIN COOPERATIVE, INC.
MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
August 1, 2025 — 2:00 PM CT — cooperative offices, Halden Junction, and by telephone

Present: President and Chair A. Sundstrom; Directors M. Halvorsen, T. Ruiz, C. Bergstrom, D. Okonkwo, F. Lindahl, P. Vasquez. Also present by invitation: O. Brandt, CFO; A. Reyes of Harwick & Sloane LLP, litigation counsel.

1. Call to order; notice; quorum. The Chair called the special meeting to order at 2:03 PM. The Secretary confirmed that notice of the special meeting was duly given and that a quorum of seven directors was present.

2. Purpose. The Chair stated that the special meeting was called to consider (a) the settlement offer received from Talvern Logistics Group LLC in the pending litigation, and (b) ratification of the amended engagement terms with litigation counsel.

3. Settlement offer. Ms. Reyes reported that by letter dated July 22, 2025, counsel for Talvern conveyed an offer of 2,100,000 dollars in full settlement of all claims, conditioned on a complete release and containing no admission of liability, open for twenty-one days. Ms. Reyes reviewed the offer against the damages components previously reported to the Board and answered directors' questions concerning litigation risk, expected costs through trial, and the spoliation issues under investigation. Director Halvorsen moved that the cooperative accept the offer as presented; Director Ruiz seconded the motion for purposes of discussion. After discussion, the Chair called the question. THE MOTION FAILED, two votes in favor (Halvorsen, Ruiz) and five opposed (Sundstrom, Bergstrom, Okonkwo, Lindahl, Vasquez). No settlement authority was granted, and the Board directed counsel to communicate the rejection of the offer and to proceed with the litigation, including the contemplated spoliation motion practice.

4. Ratification of amended engagement terms. On motion duly made and seconded, the Board voted 7-0 to ratify the First Amendment to the engagement letter with Harwick & Sloane LLP dated June 2, 2025, including the revised litigation fee budget of 1,975,000 dollars through trial stated therein.

5. Adjournment. The meeting adjourned at 3:26 PM.

Respectfully submitted,
C. Bergstrom, Secretary"}
